誰から払われるか.quote: バイヤー（買い手）は、これまで私が「顧客」と言ってきた方々です
セラー（売り手）は、これまで私が「サプライヤーパートナー」と言ってきた方々です
当社のプラットフォーム上で買い手のために製品を製造することを当社が承認したか、当社の金融サービスや消耗品の購入など、当社のセラーサービスを利用した個人または企業
オンデマンドとは要求に応じてサービスの提供を行うことを指し、マーケットプレイスとは売り手と買い手が自由に参加できる電子市場のことです
買い手は製造業の新興企業からFortune100企業のバイヤーに至るまで多岐にわたり、取引を行うバイヤーの数は43,000人以上です
また、売り手としても大規模な機械工場や職人が運営する中小企業など、様々な規模における5000以上もの企業が登録しています
AI駆動のマーケットプレイス機能を拡大し、企業の買い手と製造業のサプライヤーを接続することに焦点を当てています
企業がカスタム製造された部品を需要に応じて調達できるように、買い手と世界中のサプライヤーのネットワークを接続します
世界中の数千のサプライヤーと数万の買い手にわたるネットワークを持ち、Xometryはサプライチェーンをデジタル化し、大規模な分散型生産を可能にすることで、製造業の近代化に中心的な役割を果たしています
Xometryは、AI駆動のワークフローを採用するために、サプライヤーと買い手との信頼をどのように築いてきましたか？

What Are the Key Suppliers to Xometry?
What customers actually buy
Services for manufacturers that want to generate demand and improve their online presence.
Provider of custom manufacturing and prototyping services; competes for engineering and product-development buyers seeking rapid fulfillment.
Traditional regional machine shops and contract manufacturers
Many buyers still source directly from local or incumbent suppliers rather than through a digital platform, so offline relationships remain a real substitute to Xometry’s model.

Xometry’s marketing strategy appears to be digital-first and tightly linked to how engineers and procurement teams actually search for suppliers and parts. The company benefits from a self-serve funnel: if a buyer can get a quote online, digital acquisition economics matter a great deal.

For larger accounts, marketing likely works alongside enterprise sales through case studies, vertical messaging, account-based outreach, and relationship-building with procurement stakeholders. On the supplier-services side, marketing is effectively part of the product because manufacturers are buying customer acquisition and visibility.
Marketplace buyers

Xometry’s core marketplace buyers are engineers, product designers, operations teams, and procurement professionals that need custom parts. These customers can range from small businesses and startups to large enterprises. Public company materials indicate broad exposure across industrial end markets rather than dependence on a single vertical.
Supplier-services customers

Through Thomas, Xometry also serves industrial manufacturers and suppliers as paying customers. These companies buy digital marketing, discovery, and lead-generation services to reach industrial buyers.

The model is diversified across two customer sides: demand-side manufacturing buyers and supply-side industrial suppliers. That is strategically useful because it reduces dependence on a single monetization stream. The tradeoff is that Xometry must serve two different buying centers well: procurement and engineering on one side, marketing and business development on the other.
Buyers can upload design files, receive quotes, and place orders digitally. This is the core of Xometry’s scalable acquisition and conversion model.
Repeat customers and more complex buyers often require human support, especially when Xometry is trying to expand share of wallet.

. Marketplace includes the custom-manufacturing transaction platform, supplier network operations, and buyer-facing software and sales. Supplier Services includes Thomas, Thomasnet, and related marketing and demand-generation offerings sold to industrial suppliers.
One of the clearest growth paths is deeper penetration into existing customers by moving from ad hoc orders to repeat procurement workflows.
15. What Are the Key Suppliers to Xometry?
Xometry’s most important suppliers are not raw-material vendors in the traditional sense. They are manufacturing partners that fulfill customer orders through the marketplace.

Brand is more strategically important at Xometry than it might first appear. In custom manufacturing, software and execution drive the product experience, but Thomas gives the company a recognized industrial media and discovery brand that can attract both buyers and suppliers. That makes brand a meaningful commercial lever, not just a communications function.
The platform uses data to route jobs to suppliers based on capability, quality, timing, and economics.

This market involves a long tail of small and local suppliers that, for example, large automotive manufacturers, aerospace manufacturers, and OEMs must manage, often dealing with hundreds or even thousands of smaller specialized suppliers.

This created an opportunity for disruptor 2.0, Xometry, to enter the market. Xometry leverages a global network of over 55,000 active buyers and 3,400 active small-to-medium-sized manufacturers. With the strength of this network, Xometry’s breadth and depth of offerings greatly exceed that of Protolabs.

Xometry’s brand is increasingly perceived as the low-cost, trusted one-stop-shop platform. While brand awareness is growing on the customer side, most U.S.-based suppliers are already familiar with Xometry, and a significant number of suppliers even use Xometry to absorb overflow work.

Xometry’s management is highly strategic and aware of this problem. They continue to develop ways to integrate into both suppliers’ and customers’ workflows and ERP systems. We expect Xometry to continue to find ways to deepen integration into the operational processes of their partners, making switching less attractive.

Xometry acquired Thomas, including Thomasnet, in a deal valued at roughly $300 million, adding supplier-services revenue and a major industrial discovery platform.

The most important historical shift is that Xometry is no longer just a transaction marketplace. Since the Thomas acquisition, it has become a broader industrial platform spanning both sourcing and supplier demand generation.

21. What Major Acquisitions Has Xometry Made?
Xometry has not built its strategy around frequent large acquisitions. The major strategic exception is the 2021 acquisition of

This was the defining acquisition in Xometry’s history. It expanded the company from a transaction marketplace into supplier services, industrial discovery, and digital marketing. It also gave Xometry an owned traffic and lead-generation asset that could strengthen both sides of the platform.

The Thomas deal matters not just because of revenue added, but because it changed Xometry’s strategic shape. Through FY2024, no other publicly visible acquisition appears to match Thomas in scale or importance. Xometry therefore still looks primarily like an internally built platform, with M&A used selectively to accelerate capability rather than to assemble a conglomerate.

1c. How does Xometry plan to win?
How pricing power works
Industrial supplier listings and discovery tools.

Xometry mostly sells direct rather than through distributors. That matters strategically because direct channels let it keep the customer relationship, the demand data, and the pricing signals. It also means that sales productivity, onboarding, and customer success are important levers for growth and margin improvement.

Xometry operates with an asset-light footprint. It does not depend on a network of company-owned factories, so its geographic reach comes from offices, digital infrastructure, and its supplier network rather than from owned production plants.

The operational complexities are substantial. Quote accuracy matters because underpricing hurts margin and overpricing hurts conversion. Supplier quality and on-time performance matter because Xometry owns the customer relationship. The platform also has to balance buyer demand and supplier capacity across many processes and geographies.
2021 public listing:
AI-driven estimation supports delivery commitments and operational planning.
Each transaction can improve the data set that underpins pricing and matching decisions.
Historical pricing, part geometry, supplier performance, and conversion data improve the quote engine and matching logic.
Build country-by-country market-entry priorities, channel models, and supplier-liquidity plans for Europe.
Diagnose where instant quotes lose conversion and identify changes in pricing logic, user experience, and sales follow-up.

Given the complexity, competitor instant quoting engines will often have manual review on standby. Xometry’s advanced machine learning modeling has given them a significant head start in providing the most accurate pricing in the industry. The below expanding gross margins is an indicator that Xometry is becoming more efficient at pricing.
Xometry standard pricing: $277
Protolabs standard pricing: $550
Fictiv standard pricing: $636

Xometry’s unique positioning suggests it can evolve into a great business despite not fitting into traditional categories. The mischaracterization of Xometry’s business model as “not a marketplace” even though it enjoys network effects is a contributing factor to its mispricing.

Xometry leads the industry in using AI and machine learning for pricing, leveraging the largest data sets to train its models. Soon, Xometry will be able to price from prints through imaging. The company has the tools and data to develop a quoting engine that is 10x better than competitors. Xometry’s partnership with Google’s AI platform is a significant step in this direction.
